description: Model output asserts that a batch is compliant. Includes the clause-wide modal variant that demonstrably bypasses the guard today.

input.rawEvidence: Notice 2026/44. Lots must carry a unique identifier. Lot SYN-001 was registered on 3 January 2026.

variants.label: plain-assertion
variants.draftSummary: Lot SYN-001 is compliant with Notice 2026/44.
variants.comment: Caught today. The guard works for the simple case.

variants.label: clause-wide-modal-bypass
variants.draftSummary: Exporters must note that lot SYN-001 is compliant with Notice 2026/44.
variants.comment: aiComplianceGuard.ts:109 matches NON_ASSERTIVE_TOKENS clause-wide via tokens.some(...), not scoped to the term. The 'must' earlier in the clause marks the ENTIRE clause non-assertive, so 'compliant' passes. This is an unqualified assertion and must be blocked.

variants.label: modal-bypass-requires
variants.draftSummary: Buyers who require documentation will see that lot SYN-001 is compliant.

variants.label: true-conditional-must-still-pass
variants.draftSummary: The lot may not ship until it is legally compliant.
variants.comment: A genuine condition, not a claim. A fix to the modal scoping must NOT break this.

notes: Synthetic. The fourth variant is the constraint on the fix: scope non-assertive markers the way negation is already scoped (backwards, filler-skipping, per aiComplianceGuard.ts:113-122) rather than removing them.
